To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stress accumulation and displacement are directly proportional to the magnitude of tectonic forces, the time taken for the fault to move and the magnitude of viscosity.
the effect of the tectonically induced stresses is more significant in the case of the Kelvin type solid.
the effect of tectonic forces on the displacement and stresses in a half space is more pronounced in the region of the fault than at the surface of the half space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of an infinite surface-breaking inclined, dip-slip, locked fault in a viscoelastic half space under tectonic forces on displacement, stress and strain.
the development of a mathematical model for a long, locked, surface-breaking, dip-slip, fault in an infinite, isotropic, viscoelastic, half space.
the development of a new model of a fault system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stress and strain are not constant in the system, but are varying with time.
the stress and strain are increasing with time in the system and the displacement is increasing with time.
the stress accumulation in the viscoelastic half space due to tectonic forces is much less than in an elastic half space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stress accumulation in a viscoelastic medium is more than that of an elastic medium under similar conditions.
the viscoelasticity of the system has an important effect on the stress accumulation in the half space.
the displacement, stresses, strains and the slip velocity are increasing with time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stress accumulation is more in the vicinity of the fault than at the surface.
the displacement, stresses, and strains are found to increase with increasing time.
the viscoelastic half space is not as elastic as the elastic half space.
